stemMd: Which assessment of the draft summary is correct?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It reverses the samples; Nori exceeds Mica by3 units.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It should compare only the blank readings and ignore samples.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It is correct because equal raw readings always imply equal corrected activity.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It proves a biological difference caused by afternoon sampling.

options.label: E
options.textMd: It overlooks different run blanks; Mica’s corrected activity exceeds Nori’s by3 units.

explanationMd: Apply each run’s own correction: Mica14 and Nori11. Matching raw readings do not mean matching corrected measurements when baselines differ.

distractorRationale.c: The protocol subtracts different blanks for the two runs.
distractorRationale.b: Corrected activity requires both raw reading and blank.
distractorRationale.d: The sources prohibit biological causal conclusions from these data alone.
